evidence.quote: Fixed an issue with dry-run not capturing all errors related to teams. #2268 by @helderjs
This is caused by a bug where the underlying error is silently swallowed, preventing proper event reporting. As a result, users receive no indication that an action would have taken place.

edits.rationale: The v2.8.1 release notes list the dry-run fix for team-related errors (#2268). PR #2268 states that AKO did not emit events for team associations with AtlasProject because the error was silently swallowed, so users got no indication of the intended action. Both statements are supported by the pinned pages.

edits.old: Kubernetes API dry run with dryRun=All validates requests without persisting Kubernetes objects. AKO dry run requires actual Kubernetes resources and previews Atlas-side operations, so Kubernetes API validation alone cannot substitute for it. (high confidence)
edits.new: Kubernetes API dry run with dryRun=All runs every stage except final storage, so objects are not persisted. AKO dry run requires applying AKO custom resources to a new Kubernetes cluster, and its events report what the operator would create, update or delete in Atlas. Sources: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/api-concepts/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/operator/current/ak8so-dry-run.md

evidence.quote:
The changes

With the Atlas Kubernetes Operator Dry Run feature, you can see what Atlas Kubernetes Operator is going to change in Atlas, with those custom resources applied to the K8S cluster.
Apply Atlas Kubernetes Operator custom resources to your **new Kubernetes cluster**.

edits.old: The Atlas CLI provides atlas kubernetes dry-run, with --operatorVersion, --targetNamespace, --watchNamespace, --watch and --watchTimeout. The documented procedure uses --watch to wait; without it, the CLI exits after installation. (high confidence)
edits.new: The Atlas CLI provides atlas kubernetes dry-run, which deploys the Atlas Kubernetes Operator in dry-run mode, with --operatorVersion, --targetNamespace, --watchNamespace, --watch and --watchTimeout. --watch makes the CLI watch the command until it completes or the watch times out (--watchTimeout defaults to 120 seconds). Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-kubernetes-dry-run.md

evidence.quote: This command deploys the Atlas Kubernetes operator with the DryRun mode.
Flag that indicates whether to watch the command until it completes its execution or the watch times out.
Time in seconds until a watch times out. After a watch times out, the CLI no longer watches the command. This value defaults to 120.

statements.statement: In v2.16.0, DryRunTransport forwards GET, CONNECT, TRACE and HEAD requests, but returns DryRunError for other methods.
statements.note: Switch cases for those four methods are empty and fall through to the delegate; default returns NewDryRunError.

statements.statement: POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE become proposed create, update or delete messages.

queries: Atlas Kubernetes Operator dry run requires Kubernetes resources applied, events "Would" Atlas changes not Kubernetes API dry-run

edits.rationale: The AKO docs say dry run shows what the operator would change in Atlas and emits events only for create/update/delete verbs. The v2.16.0 transport.go forwards GET, CONNECT, TRACE and HEAD to the delegate and returns a DryRunError for every other method, mapping POST to create, PUT and PATCH to update, and DELETE to delete.
